Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b07/review-experiment-bxx7n7yr/call-405b8ab750424b13868e6f46ba0b969b/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo && command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, importlib.util, shutil
print(sys.executable)
for n in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(n, importlib.util.find_spec(n))
for n in ['pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo','gs']:
 print(n,shutil.which(n))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('pages',len(r.pages))
print('metadata',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text()
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n{t}')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts)[:42000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
for i in [5,6,9,10,11]:
 print(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n')
 print(Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
for i in range(12,18):
 print(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n')
 print(Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful problem: predicting human response times under changing environmental cues while accounting for individual differences. The two-day study provides 21,157 responses from 36 analyzed participants across four feedback conditions, forming a useful empirical resource.

The combination of task-trained representations, human-response calibration, and sequential accumulation modulation is well motivated. The representation comparison provides evidence that arithmetic-task pretraining improves prediction over the tested raw-input encodings.

Evaluation covers pooled, group-specific, individual-specific, and leave-one-participant-out settings. The hybrid model achieves lower reported aggregate MAPE than the pure DRL baseline in all four settings, providing preliminary evidence of predictive utility.
The framework diagram and procedural descriptions make the overall approach understandable. Public data and code links are provided, supporting reproducibility and further investigation.
weaknesses: The central drift-diffusion interpretation is insufficiently justified. Methods, p. 12, describes a sigmoid trajectory with an SVC probability used as its boundary, without specifying diffusion dynamics or deriving the relationship between classification probability and the accumulation boundary. This can serve as a heuristic response-time model, but its connection to established DDM mechanisms requires substantive justification.

The claimed interpretation of within-trial cognitive processes exceeds the evidence. Reward depends on final response-time agreement, and multiple accumulation trajectories can produce the same response time. Figure 7 therefore does not independently validate the inferred cognitive trajectories. Nonzero 'time pressure effects' in the no-pressure group also indicate that these corrections can absorb baseline prediction errors. Temporal-input ablations and validation under altered feedback timing would help establish whether the model captures dynamic stimulus effects.

The main comparison does not isolate the contribution of the accumulation model. The hybrid agent uses framewise CNN features, whereas the pure DRL agent receives concatenated Inception-V3 video features; action scaling, episode structure, and termination also differ. These differences confound both predictive and training-time comparisons. A matched ablation and a supervised response-time predictor receiving equivalent information are needed. Comparisons with established accumulation or sequence models would also clarify the contribution relative to the cited cognitive-modeling literature.

The evaluation protocol is underspecified for the multistage pipeline. It is unclear which no-pressure observations train the SVM baseline and whether SVC/SVR fitting and preprocessing occur strictly within every training split, including LOPO. Without this information, readers cannot verify that held-out human responses are excluded throughout the pipeline or that the learned corrections isolate pressure effects.

The predictive improvements need uncertainty estimates. For example, MAPE changes from 0.3034 to 0.2999 in pooled evaluation and from 0.3037 to 0.2905 in LOPO. These are encouraging but modest differences, and no confidence intervals or clearly described variability across repeated model-training runs establish their reliability. Participant-level paired comparisons would be particularly informative.

The behavioral conclusions require more careful statistical qualification. Only seven analyzed participants belong to the random-feedback group, and three participants were excluded as extreme outliers without an operational exclusion criterion. The stated use of paired post-hoc tests between groups also needs explanation because the groups contain different participants. Nonsignificant accuracy effects do not establish that accuracy is unaffected by pressure.

Important implementation details are missing from the manuscript, including the sigmoid parameterization and complete accumulation update, the value of the perturbation factor lambda, and numerical thresholds for the adaptive feedback rule. The treatment of responses beyond the model's ten-second limit also needs clarification. These omissions hinder assessment and reproduction despite the provided code link.
